_meta.title: Public-only reference joint-angle trajectories for a 110+ mph driver swing (synthetic interpolation between published keyframes)
_meta.status: SYNTHETIC reference built from published keyframes, peak speeds and peak timings. NOT measured curves. No published source gives a full time-normalised curve for a 110+ mph group. Values at 120 and 130 mph are extrapolated (no published joint-angle study above ~112 mph with angles).
_meta.right_handed_convention: Rotation channels: + = toward target (open), backswing negative (RH). Time t in seconds, t = 0 at ball impact, negative before. phase = (t + T_downswing) / T_downswing: 0 at top of backswing, 1 at impact.

left_handed_mirror_rule.summary: Express everything in golfer ROLES (trail/lead), not physical left/right (docs/HANDEDNESS.md). Rotation about the vertical axis (pelvis_rotation, thorax_rotation, x_factor; env chest_yaw / pelvis yaw): NEGATE for a left-hander (backswing positive, impact negative) if the env's own handedness flip is NOT already applied; ResidualGolfEnv already multiplies the chest_yaw target by -1 for handedness='left', so feed this file's RH values to the env's handedness layer and do not negate twice. Sagittal/planar angles (elbow flexion, wrist set angle, arm-to-trunk elevation): NO sign change. Roles: env right_* = TRAIL arm, left_* = LEAD arm for both handednesses. +y is the golfer's left (RH) / handedness-mirrored lateral in the env.
left_handed_mirror_rule.status: rule restated from docs/HANDEDNESS.md and data/mirror_references.py (negate pelvis/thorax/x-factor; planar flexion invariant). Not tested against this file. UNVERIFIED for env roll joints.

env_mapping_summary.pelvis_rotation: G1 env pelvis_yaw_joint; NO pelvis yaw in the simple env (v3/v4_power) -- use as thorax-minus-pelvis only if the Trainer's env has it
env_mapping_summary.thorax_rotation: simple env chest_yaw (+-45 deg v3, +-60 deg v4_power); G1 waist_yaw_joint. NOTE: -103 deg thorax at top exceeds chest_yaw range +-60 deg; env chest_yaw is likely pelvis-relative (an X-factor-like quantity), so consider x_factor channel instead (UNVERIFIED)
env_mapping_summary.x_factor: pelvis-relative thorax rotation = the likely match for env chest_yaw if the pelvis is fixed (UNVERIFIED)
env_mapping_summary.elbows: env right_elbow (trail, actuated), left_elbow (lead, unactuated in simple env)
env_mapping_summary.wrists: env right_wrist (trail hinge); no lead wrist in simple env. w = 90 - interior_angle_deg (repo note), absolute values inconsistent with env contact solution

sampling_grid.note: t < -T_downswing is the end of the backswing: angle HELD at the top keyframe (extrapolation, not published). t > 0 is follow-through: speed decays exponentially with tau=0.05 s (ASSUMED). Published support exists ONLY for -T_downswing <= t <= 0.

speed_scaling_rule.angles: Top and impact keyframe angles are held FIXED across speed classes (ASSUMED). Basis: X-factor is not correlated with club speed within homogeneous skilled groups (Kwon 2013 abstract, kseq-v2 d_kwon_no_correlation; Parker 2018 beta -0.24), but this is not evidence that every joint angle is speed-invariant.
speed_scaling_rule.downswing_duration: T(v) = 0.253 s - 0.0025 s per (m/s) * (v - 49.35 m/s) (between-group Bourgain-based slope; default). Alternative within-group Madrid slope -0.00596 s per m/s gives shorter T (see 'downswing_duration_s_alt_within'). Anchor 253+-26 ms at 110.4 mph (Madrid 2020). Cite: kseq-v2 'downswing_duration_by_chs'. Above ~116 mph UNSUPPORTED extrapolation.
speed_scaling_rule.pelvis_thorax_peak_speed: Madrid anchor at 110.4 mph + within-group slope (13.2 and 13.83 deg/s per m/s; regression-diluted lower bounds; kseq-v2 derived). Extrapolated above ~116 mph.
speed_scaling_rule.arm_elbow_wrist_peak_speed: Linear in club speed from Zheng pro values with ASSUMED reference 109 mph (CHS unreported; same assumption as kinematic_sequence_torque_reference.json). ASSUMED.
speed_scaling_rule.peak_timing: pelvis/thorax: ms before impact held constant (ASSUMED); arm/elbow/wrist: fixed fraction of downswing (Zheng, secondary).
speed_scaling_rule.speed_at_impact: pelvis/thorax: ratio to peak from Madrid held constant (ASSUMED). Arm/elbow/wrist: ASSUMED ratios (0.5-0.95), no published values.

interpolation.method: angle = angle_top + integral of PCHIP speed profile; speed ramp P*s^k to the cited peak at the cited peak time, smoothstep tail to the speed at impact; k solved so top->impact change equals the cited keyframes
interpolation.kind: monotone (speed >= 0 so angle is monotone between top and impact)
interpolation.why_not_plain_pchip: plain PCHIP through only top/impact keyframes would give a near-linear sweep with peak speed ~ mean speed (e.g. ~330 deg/s for the pelvis vs cited peak 394), which contradicts the published kinematic sequence

tolerance_bands.sd_angle_deg: linear in phase between keyframe SDs (derived; SDs are between-subject at the keyframe, not along the curve)
tolerance_bands.timing_term: band_total_deg = sqrt(sd_angle^2 + (0.026 s * |omega|)^2); 0.026 s = Madrid downswing-duration SD, a time-alignment allowance (derived)
tolerance_bands.other_channels: No published SD retrieved: sd_deg is null and band is null. Use tolerance_deg_recommended (ASSUMED).

recommended_soft_reward_usage.status: SUGGESTION, not tuned or tested in any training run
recommended_soft_reward_usage.window: downswing only: -T_downswing <= t <= -0.01 s (phase 0..~0.96). Weight 0 before the top and after impact (no published support).
recommended_soft_reward_usage.form: r_t = sum_c w_c * exp(-0.5 * (err_c / tol_c)^2), err_c = env_angle_c(t) - ref_c(t); use rotation channels first
recommended_soft_reward_usage.total_weight: low: keep the whole prior <= ~5% of the per-step reward (suggested 0.02-0.05), annealed to 0 once speed at impact and the sequence reward are met, so the prior can not override ball-flight rewards

lead_wrist_set_angle.note: use release magnitude/timing only; absolute value does not map to env w

recommended_soft_reward_usage.use_timing_not_absolutes: For elbow/wrist, prefer rewarding the phase of release (peak-speed time as fraction of downswing) and the change in angle, because env contact geometry fixes absolute values (see lead_wrist_set_angle mapping_note).

_meta.license_note: Numbers are published facts/means cited to their papers; the curves are original constructions by this repo (MIT). Papers are cited, not reproduced; Madrid 2020 is CC BY (attribution given). No third-party data tables are copied wholesale. See docs/PUBLIC_JOINT_TRAJECTORIES_110PLUS.md.

sources.madrid2020: Madrid, Avalos, Levine, Tuttle, Becker, Kwon. Appl Sci 10(17):5728 (2020), open access CC BY. 66 skilled males, driver CHS 110.4+-4.8 mph, 500 Hz optical (values via data/references/kinematic_sequence_torque_reference_v2.json, tag fetched-full)
sources.cheetham2008: Cheetham PJ, Rose GA, Hinrichs RN, Neal RJ, Mottram RE, Hurrion PD, Vint PF. Science and Golf V, 2008, 30-36. 19 PGA tour pros, driver, mean CHS 109 mph, 240 Hz electromagnetic (peak-timing values via kinematic_sequence_torque_reference.json)
sources.cheetham2014: Cheetham PJ. Doctoral dissertation, Arizona State University, Aug 2014 (philcheetham.com/media/Phillip-Cheetham-Doctoral-Dissertation-2014.pdf). 94 PGA/European tour pros, driver, mean CHS 48.4 m/s = 108.3 mph, 240 Hz electromagnetic; Tables 8-9, Study 2 text. Full text read
sources.zheng2008a: Zheng N, Barrentine SW, Fleisig GS, Andrews JR. Int J Sports Med 29(6):487-493 (2008). 18 professional males, driver, 240 Hz optical; CHS not reported. Abstract read (trunk 60+-7 deg at top); remaining top/impact/timing values are SECONDARY, read from lecture notes (Lehman, MSKPlus course, Mar 2012, thebodymechanic.ca) quoting the paper, not checked against the primary table
sources.zheng2008b: Zheng N, Barrentine SW, Fleisig GS, Andrews JR. Int J Sports Med 29:965-970 (2008). 25 PGA + 25 LPGA pros; abstract read: pelvis orientation at top PGA 42+-7 deg, pelvis rotation at impact PGA -42+-12 deg (their sign convention)
sources.kseq_v2_derived: data/references/kinematic_sequence_torque_reference_v2.json 'derived': Madrid within-group slopes (deg/s per m/s) pelvis 13.2, thorax 13.83; downswing-duration slopes -5.96 (within-group Madrid) and -2.5 (between-group Bourgain 2020) ms per m/s; regression-diluted lower bounds, extrapolation above ~116 mph unsupported

x_factor.description: X-factor = thorax rotation minus pelvis rotation (derived from the two channels above); + = thorax more toward target (open) than pelvis; in RH convention the top value is negative of the usual positive 'X-factor' magnitude (-61 here = 61 deg of torso-pelvis separation, closed)

source_keyframes.note: X-factor at top 61+-9 deg (functional swing plane); defines the thorax top keyframe; also max 62+-8

thorax(27) - pelvis(41) = -14 deg (closed) by construction; Madrid 2020 measured X-factor at impact 9+-8 deg (different sign convention/method; magnitude agreement within 1 SD of Madrid); Meister 2011 5-iron pros 24-33 deg; Chu 2010 12.3+-9.1

x_factor.interpolation: difference of the two integrated channels (not independently interpolated)
x_factor.confidence: medium-low: top from Madrid (n=66), impact is a difference of two means from different studies

derived_checks.note: Peak-timing sequence in the curves follows the published order for pelvis (-87 ms) -> thorax (-84 ms): the 3 ms gap is within published SD (18-25 ms) and contradicts Cheetham 2008 (68 ms for thorax); sequence order is not guaranteed by this file.
